([[Bradenton, Florida]]) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | highlights = }} '''Anfernee Simons''' (born June 8, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played prep basketball for [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]]. He is first American to enter an [[NBA draft]] directly after graduation from high school since the league first implemented age restriction rules in 2005.{{cn|date=May 2018}} ==High school career== Simons first attended [[Edgewater High School]] in [[Orlando]], [[Florida]], where during his sophomore year he averaged 17.8 points, 4.6 assists, 2.4 rebounds, and 1 steal per game in 30 games.{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/anfernee-simons/JOekE2tmEeS00gAmVebEWg/gendersport/basketball-stats.htm|title=Anfernee Simons' High School Basketball Stats|website=MaxPreps.com}} During his junior year he transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida|Montverde]],{{cite web|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-hs-anfernee-simons-basketball-prospect-0706-20160705-story.html|title=Anfernee Simons back to Edgewater with bigger game|first=Buddy|last=Collings|publisher=}} but after being a bench player, returned to Edgewater with the intention of holding his name back from college consideration for a year.{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2017/11/19/16674672/anfernee-simons-nba-draft-2018-recruiting-louisville-florida|title=Who is Anfernee Simons, the top-10 recruit who will enter the 2018 NBA Draft through a loophole?|publisher=}} He graduated from Edgewater in 2017, averaging 23.8 points, 7.2 rebounds, 4.2 assists, 1.8 steals, and 0.5 blocks per game in 20 games played in his last year there. Then, because of his reclassification in the Class of 2018, he attended the [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida|Bradenton]] for a postgraduate year, although he had previously expressed interest in spending that year at the West Oaks Academy in Orlando instead.{{cite web|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-sp-hs-varsity-report-0712-story.html|title=Former Edgewater star Anfernee Simons headed to IMG Academy|first=Buddy|last=Collings|publisher=}} During the summer of 2017, he also played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team]].{{cite web|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/philly-hoops/duke-basketball-cam-reddish-westtown-school-under-19-world-championships-20170908.html|title=Duke-bound Cam Reddish and his crazy summer | Mike Jensen|website=philly.com|accessdate=2017-12-27}} Simons was rated as a five-star recruit and was ranked as the 7th best player in the 2018 class by [[247Sports.com]].{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.pennlive.com/news/article/-4015483637851346468/westtown-star-cameron-reddish-ascends-to-no-1-in-recruiting-services-rankings/|title=Westtown star Cameron Reddish ascends to No. 1 in recruiting service’s rankings|website=PennLive.com|accessdate=2017-12-27}} Originally, he planned to enter the [[University of Louisville]],{{cite web|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2735523-5-stars-anfernee-simons-courtney-ramey-decommit-from-louisville-amid-scandal|title=Anfernee Simons, Courtney Ramey Decommit from Louisville Amid Scandal|first=Adam|last=Wells|publisher=}} but as a result of the [[2015 University of Louisville basketball sex scandal|basketball sex scandal of 2015]] at the university and its involvement in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]], he ultimately decommitted from Louisville, saying that he was most interested in the [[University of South Carolina]], [[North Carolina State University]], the [[University of Tennessee]], and the [[University of Florida]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Anfernee-Simons-to-consider-NBA-Draft-but-likely-headed-to-college-110683713|title=Anfernee Simons to consider NBA Draft, but likely headed to college|publisher=}} In January 2018, he then said that he was "most likely" going to bypass college and enter the [[2018 NBA Draft]], albeit without hiring an agent.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2018/01/17/anfernee-simons-nba-draft-img-academy-tennessee-nc-state-louisville|title=Anfernee Simons's big draft decision is imminent|publisher=}} In March 2018 he confirmed his decision,{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22869177/anfernee-simons-declares-nba-draft-forgoing-collegiate-eligibility|title=Simons declares for NBA draft, forgoes college|publisher=}} and later removed his name from the 2018 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite web|url=http://sportando.basketball/en/usa/high-school/269271/anfernee-simons-withdraws-his-name-from-nike-hoop-summit-and-jordan-brand-classic.html|title=Anfernee Simons withdraws his name from Nike Hoop Summit and Jordan Brand Classic|publisher=}} Simons was one of the 69 players invited to the 2018 [[NBA Draft Combine]] that year.{{cn|date=May 2018}} {{As of|2018|03|20}}, [[ESPN]] ranked him as the 19th likeliest draft pick overall.{{cite news |first=Ben |last=Roberts |url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article206352374.html|title=One of the top basketball recruits in the country is jumping straight to the NBA| newspaper=Lexington Herald-Leader |date=March 22, 2018 }} ==Personal life== Simons was given the name Anfernee due to his parents, Charles and Tameka, being fans of the [[Orlando Magic]] and naming him after former player [[Anfernee Hardaway]].{{cite web|url=https://heavy.com/sports/2018/03/anfernee-simons-nba-draft-who-mock-highlights/|title=Anfernee Simons Is the NBA Draft’s Man of Mystery|first=Jonathan|last=Adams|date=22 March 2018|website=Heavy.com}}{{cite web|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2766108-hs-star-anfernee-simons-decides-cbb-isnt-for-him-but-is-he-ready-for-the-nba|title=HS Star Anfernee Simons Decides CBB Isn't for Him, but Is He Ready for the NBA?|first=Jason|last=King|website=Bleacher Report}} Hardaway coached Simons during a Team USA Basketball training camp. ==References== {{reflist}}
